* Tune media fragment readiness timeout and cap WebM capture timeouts

- Create timestamp-derived WebM fragments with fresh rendering resources
- Keep existing in-flight cancellation behavior while removing shared mutable DOM state between instances
- Prevent races where concurrent/stale renders could draw to the same canvas or mutate the same video element

* Harden WebM frame-rate sampling timeout and delta collection

- Replace fixed sampling timeout with playback-rate-aware calculation
- Keep sampling timeout capped at 3000ms maximum
- Introduce base and max sampling timeout constants for clearer tuning
- Ignore implausibly small media-time deltas based on max capture frame rate
- Prevent duplicate/near-duplicate frame callbacks from inflating sample count

* Refactor WebM video state management with reusable VideoStateGuard

- Add SavedVideoState and VideoStateGuard helpers to centralize save/restore behavior
- Capture playbackRate, muted, volume, onerror, onended, and optional preservesPitch in one place
- Replace duplicated manual property save/restore in _renderWebm with guard apply/restore

Fix inferTracks leaking basename and tracks across soft-navigation (#1023)

* inferTracks had two related defects that could surface as wrong
   data attached to the current video after the user soft-navigates
   within an SPA.
    - First, basename was stored in a single closure-scoped variable.
      With waitForBasename: false (which most streaming page scripts
      use), the final dispatch read whatever value happened to be set,
      so a previous video's title could end up on the current one if
      the new basename lookup had not completed (or had failed) by
      dispatch time. Add a basenameByPath map mirroring the existing
      subtitlesByPath, written by setBasename and read by the current
      pathname at dispatch and in ready(). Extend garbageCollect to
      clean it too.
    - Second, the addTrack and setBasename callbacks passed to onRequest
      both read window.location.pathname at the moment the async
      onRequest callback resolved, which meant a soft-navigation between
      request-start and callback-resolution would file the old video's
      data under the new pathname. Capture requestPath once when the
      asbplayer-get-synced-data handler fires, and have both callbacks
      write to that captured path. Reads (ready and final dispatch)
      still use the current pathname, so asbplayer always gets data for
      whichever video the user is actually watching.
 * Also guard the partial basename dispatch on
   requestPath === window.location.pathname, so an old request can
   no longer fire a basename-only event for a video that is no
   longer current.
 * Affects all inferTracks users, including direct callers such as
   Bandai Channel, Bilibili, Disney+, Hulu, NRK TV, SVT Play, and
   TVer, plus page scripts that go through
   inferTracksFromInterceptedMpd,
   inferTracksFromInterceptedMpdViaXMLHTTPRequest, or
   inferTracksFromInterceptedM3u8. The MPD/M3U8 helpers call
   setBasename(document.title) internally, so they exercise the
   same code path.
 * Separately, fix an existing bug in poll(): the early
   resolve(true) on first-test success had no return, so the
   function still scheduled one wasted setTimeout and one extra
   test() call before exiting. Add the return to short-circuit
   the loop. Drop the unused reject parameter from the Promise
   constructor at the same time.
 * Known limitation: the onJson path (Bandai Channel, Bilibili, TVer)
   still reads window.location.pathname at JSON.parse time. The parse
   hook has no reference to the originating fetch, so a response in
   flight across a soft-navigation can still attribute data to the
   wrong path on those three sites. Fixing it needs per-site changes
   that key on a stable payload identifier (the Hulu page script uses
   content_eab_id for exactly this reason), and is left for follow-up
   if it surfaces in practice.

Stop subtitle picker resetting while user is interacting with it (#1026)

* Stop subtitle picker resetting while user is interacting with it
 * Some players (Hulu in particular) fire loadedmetadata on an
   internal timer while the video is paused, and separately call
   video.play() on a setTimeout. When the subtitle picker is open
   with an in-progress user selection, both behaviors disturb it.
 * The cyclic loadedmetadata causes asbplayer to re-fetch synced
   data and re-run the auto-sync evaluation, which wipes any
   in-progress user selection in the open picker and clears
   subtitles already loaded into the player. The setTimeout play()
   un-pauses the video despite asbplayer's _prepareShow having
   paused it via this._context.pause().
 * For most sites, loadedmetadata appears to correspond to actual
   video changes rather than cyclic blob rotation while paused, and
   players do not auto-play paused videos. Hulu is the exception
   observed in practice. Verified by probing video.play and seeing
   Hulu's app.js call it via setTimeout.
 * In binding.ts, the videoChangeListener body is now gated on the
   picker being open AND on the same pathname as when it opened. The
   listener still updates the registered video src but skips
   requestSubtitles and _resetSubtitles while that gate holds. On a
   true soft-navigation, it falls through and refreshes.
 * In video-data-sync-controller.ts:
    - New public pickerVisible and openedPathname getters expose
      picker state (visibility, and the pathname captured when the
      picker opened) to the binding without poking at private fields.
    - requestSubtitles returns early when the picker is open on the
      same pathname, so cyclic events can no longer clear synced
      state while the user is interacting. If called with the picker
      open on a different pathname (a soft-navigation), it dismisses
      the stale picker and proceeds with the fresh fetch.
    - _setSyncedData gates the auto-sync apply, failure-prompt
      show(), and trailing updateState on this._frame.hidden. A
      wasLoading exception (captured from _syncedData?.subtitles
      being undefined before assignment) lets the picker transition
      from loading state to populated the first time tracks arrive
      after the dialog opened pre-data.
    - _prepareShow captures window.location.pathname and installs a
      play event listener on the video that immediately re-pauses.
      Both are cleaned up from _hideAndResume (the pathname cleared,
      the listener removed via a new _cleanupPlayBlocker helper). A
      new explicit cancel handler now calls _hideAndResume instead of
      relying on cancel falling through the default dataWasSynced=true
      path implicitly.
    - unbind now also calls _cleanupPlayBlocker and clears the
      captured pathname, so neither the play listener nor the
      picker-session marker leaks if the controller is torn down
      with the picker still open.
 * Pairs with the Hulu subtitle rewrite. The bug fixed here was
   latent until that rewrite made synced-data responses reliable on
   repeated requests, exposing this picker-state behavior.

* Address review feedback: pickerVisible, optional chaining, _context.pause()
 * Swap this._frame.hidden to !this.pickerVisible at the three call
   sites in _setSyncedData (auto-sync apply, failure-prompt show, and
   the trailing updateState branch). Same semantic, but the code now
   reads as the actual rule (do not auto-sync or show prompts while the
   picker is open, except for the loading-to-populated update) instead
   of directly checking the frame's hidden flag.
 * Also swap this._openedPathname to this.openedPathname at the read
   site in requestSubtitles, for the same naming-consistency reason.
   binding.ts already consumes the getter, so this makes the
   controller's internal reads consistent.
 * Drop the redundant clientIfLoaded !== undefined checks and use
   optional chaining at the call sites. Argument evaluation
   short-circuits with the chain, so _buildModel is not invoked when
   the client is not loaded.
 * Switch _playBlocker to call this._context.pause() instead of
   this._context.video.pause(), so the play blocker uses the same
   site-aware pause abstraction as the rest of the controller.

* Stop subtitle reset on loadedmetadata when already synced
 * The picker-open guard added in an earlier commit suppresses
   reset+refetch only while the picker is visible. With the picker
   closed and subtitles loaded, loadedmetadata still ran
   _resetSubtitles and requestSubtitles, clearing the side panel for
   the duration of the round-trip through the page script and the
   subtitle fetch.
 * binding.ts now tracks the href at which subtitles were last
   successfully synced (set in _updateSubtitles, cleared in
   _resetSubtitles and unbind). videoChangeListener short-circuits
   the reset+refetch when a loadedmetadata fires for that same href.
 * All same-video identity checks switch from
   window.location.pathname to window.location.href, so hash-based
   video identity (Emby/Jellyfin via syncAllowedAtHash in
   pages.json) is handled correctly. The picker-open guard in
   binding.ts and the soft-navigation detection in requestSubtitles
   use the same comparison.
 * An earlier commit characterized Hulu's loadedmetadata trigger as
   cyclic blob URL rotation while paused. Direct observation in a
   follow-up instrumentation session shows the pattern is narrower:
    - Hulu fires loadedmetadata 2-3 times during initial player
      boot (first ~5 seconds) as the MediaSource blob URL is
      established for the main content stream, independent of user
      input.
    - Hulu can rotate the blob URL ~10 seconds after a pause, which
      fires loadedmetadata and also triggers an auto-play() from
      the same setTimeout callback. In testing this fired for the
      first two pauses of a session but not for subsequent pauses,
      including pauses of 117 seconds and longer. The gating
      condition is not fully characterized but appears tied to
      early-session state, plausibly initial DRM license or
      manifest refresh.
    - Repeated rotations only manifest when something keeps
      re-pausing the video. asbplayer's playBlocker while the
      picker is open does exactly that. Outside that re-pause loop,
      each qualifying pause produces exactly one rotation, after
      which Hulu's auto-play() resumes playback.
    - A pause shorter than ~10 seconds cancels the timer cleanly.
 * The synced-state guard added here is the correct fix regardless
   of how narrow the natural trigger turns out to be, because it
   short-circuits the reset+refetch path before any site-specific
   timing matters. To verify: dispatching a loadedmetadata event on
   the video element from the page console no longer clears loaded
   subtitles.

Fix Hulu silently dropping non-first subtitle tracks (#1027)

* The dedup filter in extractSubtitleTracks compared each existing
   subtitle's own label to its own language. Since label is set to
   the original webvtt key and language is set to its lowercased
   form, any first-added track with an already-lowercase key (e.g.
   "en") satisfied the filter and caused every subsequent language
   to be skipped. Hulu's /v6/playlist webvtt object uses lowercase
   keys, so only the first listed language ever made it through.
   That was typically English, with Spanish and others silently
   dropped.
 * Replace the custom plumbing with a window.fetch wrapper that
   observes Hulu's own /v6/playlist response, plus a DOM scrape of
   [data-testid="player-metadata"] for the basename. This avoids
   the previous architecture's duplicate POST to /v6/playlist,
   whose response carried session tokens (sauron_id, sauron_token)
   and risked registering a second Hulu playback session against
   the user's account. The /upnext GET is also no longer needed.
 * Key cached tracks by the entityId parsed from the response's
   content_eab_id field rather than by window.location.pathname.
   Hulu's in-player next-video button fires the new video's
   /v6/playlist several hundred milliseconds before it updates the
   URL via replaceState, so pathname at fetch time points at the
   previous video. Keying by entityId from the response itself is
   the reliable identifier for this flow.
 * Also add an ignoreVideoElements config in pages.json to filter
   out Hulu's VideoPreviewPlayer element (the up-next preview
   player). It has a valid blob `src` and would otherwise become a
   second binding, triggering asbplayer's multi-video element
   picker on every subtitle picker invocation.
 * Tradeoff versus the previous implementation: the new flow
   passively observes Hulu's fetch, so if the page script injects
   after Hulu has already fetched the playlist, subtitles are
   unavailable until the next fetch fires (typically on episode
   navigation). The old active re-fetch handled this, but at the
   cost of a duplicate POST and session-token risk.

Back-fill missing page settings on read to fix Firefox video detection

Chrome deep-merges object-typed default values into stored values when
reading from chrome.storage, while Firefox only fills top-level missing
keys. A stored streamingPages blob missing a newly added page key (e.g.
crunchyroll in 1.21.0) therefore resolves with undefined page settings
on Firefox, throwing a TypeError in the video content script's page
config merge and preventing video bindings from being created on every
site.

Preserve the invariant that page settings contain every known key by
back-filling missing or malformed entries from defaults in
ensureConsistencyOnRead, mirroring the existing keyBindSet pattern, on
both read and import paths.
